item.title: Appreciation vs Appropriation: Reconciliation in Practice - by Toronto Public Library — Mon Sep 21, 6:00 PM — Spadina Road Public Library
item.description:
More info: https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/events/6a87439baafa6100295decf9
Hosted by Toronto Public Library (https://www.torontopubliclibrary.ca)
Join Dr. Ruth Green for a discussion that explores the line between Indigenous cultural appreciation and cultural appropriation. Using real world examples like artwork, jewelry, clothing, and pow wows, Ruth will examine how non-Indigenous people can engage respectfully with Indigenous cultures and make informed, respectful choices.

item.title: Coffee and Conversation — Tue Sep 22, 9:30 AM — Malvern
item.description:
Enjoy some light refreshments, and informal discussion about services in the neighbourhood. Get to know your local library staff and let us know what information and resources you would like to access at the library and in the community. item.title: Moving Stories: Arts-based movement class for older adults — Tue Sep 22, 10:00 AM — Leaside
item.description:
Tiger princess dance projects , a non-profit contemporary dance company, brings you a free custom designed arts-based movement class for older adults. Join Artistic Director Yvonne Ng and her team of professional artists in a fun, healthy, and exciting arts program, Moving Stories . These free classes offer an introduction into the enriching world of art and creativity through movement and music. These activities have proven to improve circulation, retain joint mobility, promote mental stimulation, improve posture and coordination, and build strength and balance. No previous movement experience required. Suggested Age: 60 + Go at your own pace, modifications encouraged Exercises can be modified for seated movement and/or standing
Source: Toronto Public Library — Older Adults

item.title: Diaries of Mark Robinson Algonquin Park Ranger 1908-1936 — Tue Sep 22, 2:00 PM — Fairview
item.description: Dr. Gregory Klages presents Algonquin Diaries, comprising the diary entries of Mark Robinson about life in Algonquin Park in the early 20th century. For over three decades, Robinson served as ranger, acting Park Superintendent, and officer in the Canadian Expeditionary Force. Throughout, he maintained daily diaries in which he recorded his experiences of significant social, political, cultural and environmental events. Dr. Klages is the author of The Many Deaths of Tom Thompson: Separating Fact from Fiction , a Writers' Trust of Canada Best Books 2016. item.title: Death Café — Tue Sep 22, 6:30 PM — Guildwood

Attendees who are blind or with low vision are invited to explore the tactile surface while listening to Rennie’s own authored description of the work. With the goal of supporting broader uptake across galleries and museums, Rennie has made the device schematics open source and co-developed “Artcessible,” a QR-based smartphone app for accessing audio description, while continuing to critically examine the economic and material barriers embedded in mainstream tech solutions. item.description: Surviving Dementia Care is a compassionate and insightful guide for anyone navigating the challenging journey of caring for a loved one with dementia. Drawing on research from information studies, literary studies, and interviews with family caregivers, this book reimagines dementia care – not as a set of skills to master, but as a deeply human experience to endure and understand. ​Author and Professor Emeritus D. Grant Campbell will address the experiences of families who are caring for a loved one who is living with dementia, including the various points of stress, as well as the various points of joy, and ways in which caregivers learn to survive the experience. Major topics include understanding the diagnosis, communicating with the loved one, choosing an assisted living facility, and using music and the arts as a means of connection. item.description:
The Arts department of the Toronto Reference Library presents a screening of Perfect Days. Perfect Days is a 2023 drama film directed by Wim Wenders. It tells the story of Hirayama, a middle-aged man living a quiet, deeply structured life in Tokyo. He works as a cleaner for the city's public restrooms, but finds profound contentment and grace in his simple daily routines.
